scope: Genuine generation participant recovery custody, continued native operation, exact original retention, existing-store cold reopening and explicit authenticated author reconnect. Not room activation, independent comment/server generations, platform qualification or V1 approval.

source.postQualificationChanges: Only the compatibility boundary, operation verification guide, V1 checkpoint note and this scoped record.

implementation.nativeOrigin: Actual readonly original native replay and canonical verifySegmentedRecoveryOrigin before current-source constructor/autosave; both document and paired review journal prefixes and generation ancestry are checked. No AST equality or metadata-only adoption.
implementation.custody: Genuine recovered owner, private managed-source ports and four distinct dedicated names. Retain exact original plus prepared intent, publish operational intent, then transfer native/source ownership. Failed publication can retry with the held original or cold resume.
implementation.currentStores: Noncreating exact-schema source and upload opens. Missing acknowledged files, unrelated native history and changed original intent refuse rather than initialize, repair or overwrite. Prepared intent requires the exact original; published intent admits native descendants.
implementation.retention: Original local versions and acknowledged relay progress remain required. Original immutable uploads and acknowledged receipts remain; epochs and attempts may advance. New generations, comments, versions and uploads remain usable. Explicit stop-retrying and packet eviction keep their existing semantics.
implementation.currentAuthority: Fresh host authority, read-only/review policy and native factories remain mandatory on every resume. No credentials, grants or network readiness are restored from the file. Connections and uploads remain explicit.
implementation.handoffRepair: Distinguish readable backup source from live managed custody. Recheck current authority and managed source after awaited release before returning editable owners. Failed post-release authority retains a readable original with cleanup-only ownership, not another handoff opportunity.
